04BDA428A32E4EA2B1B373871FE6D077.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole (the whole can be a set of objects), including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

A66F63742BE344A49B7DD63DC84BAB3A.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

6CB0BAA5AD214679BDAE321A3016F65A.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

77B833B5AAF3405B8022DDCE534102B4.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

7EB85A59C87E4F44A41350DC2B1BAB63.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.

1C5C74BE4D0C4C89BC76B0AD112B3505.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

6562DC68BF7143D08411E2AF0F3967E0.description: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

9E5297EDBCC643769CD21550271F2FD8.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the zero on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

6736AF3179AA4836BB292B166F1FC8AE.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

52D8EC78FE5443DEA94206C81F55402D.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

C6559B49D8634F7F9393D5442D581FCE.description: Apply the formula V = l × w × h and V = B × h (where B stands for the area of the base) for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

2983E164495E4C978DC8F86DF86E273A.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

E9A81568AAE1465A984E9E8BB9500833.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.

CC50FFFF75F64281A47ABB47D21EACC0.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in., cubic ft., and non-standard units.

17AB401DD63F4E17A7E255AA0A0285A2.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

785D530D6C044751B4FF52C95F4A55D6.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

B831FF927FD94F8F929F329F7A99A4C0.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

1F4220BECB0A4EECA515CB94C21A179B.description: Geometric measurement: Understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

4FFB6F049B1D46738A08BD4AB7FF291F.description: Make a line plot (dot plot) to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit. Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plot (dot plot).

36E9B94598F34D6F9A8D5AF15C48C0BE.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.

51D5CEF9B0384FA98470E8C5AD3A87EB.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

9AC3A94153614C45BBEFE2FB0EFA5AEC.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction and between multiplication and division; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

7BEEEBC4D6DD41AEB8BA4D67C1123D3B.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

5C1595495F2A49B7886E66CFD0A93FDB.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers. (Include two-digit x four-digit numbers and, three-digit x three-digit numbers) using the standard algorithm.

2D7FCF42D4C24A009064830704276626.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

FD546FA4374B439E9218CF53684BCB4E.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

E97DC598938C407C8302C6CF8B2BEE22.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

205BBF6CE78D4E9E9EFFF16CBFCDFEEC.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1∕10) + 9 × (1∕100) + 2 × (1∕1000).

5FE91608B4C0483CA5ECF34C3D1F7679.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

368703B2D4A44BC8B13C9A40248B1876.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

6CEDD7C2D0AE426780560F3B0AE981A0.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, including decimals, a digit in any place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1∕10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

6C8D9F34D5F5449F8A495B38F47529F8.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

DE1FC0A21F00472DBA2552FC4D168EFA.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

D846A4A3D9E24577912A1E2D300106BE.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

279103009EBE439A90A84EB1AD5684FB.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols, e.g.,(6 x 30) + (6 x ½).

A574CFB8530C45B3AA0B4E0071C4B7D4.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

347341EAA4DE41E298041952FF9BFC2B.description: Look for and make use of structure.

94B019214851489FA991EA6C73CA8536.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

A25F28F6AE5F49E59EED744E60B719C0.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Rhode Island Core Standards for Mathematics

11B70CCEC75049E4868D4D2306AAB988.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

6DA7D0E19E0C4CC1A88A97B72EEB8A3D.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median, and/or mean) and variability (range and/or interquartile range), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

6B519728B101401DAF27585A7C0DDB84.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

A3A89972F6E64F628E4D0E203E481579.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

B06831B7EFE343DB9081A213FFAC2DEE.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

3633D37B7C4A45F59954567C2634C0A8.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

3CEFFEF370784880AADE0DE466FD0C31.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution, which can be described by its center (median, mean, and/or mode), spread (range, interquartile range), and overall shape.

23373353EFDE40EFA05551E50FBDF551.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

FA518D7DE710431FA834109E3992AA60.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

491775C36649414A8523838437C75928.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

101E30686CB04B69A591968F2A4D3BC9.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

D0584703090945C58340CFBCCA6CA73A.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q, and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

4866EC9E61EE42C3AC9CEF32375CC1F0.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

B4C598F03120420AA5C7AB26EDCFFCBF.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: Which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

0536284F778E4B4EA6D98A207D01D2DA.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

833325FD75F04AC995D3C160ADFA6DFD.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).

04BE320C4BB24A129B648383A0E49997.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

2527DD730B004B9D9F9D6A2AC4EE97D5.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

F9B0F84D16184307865CEA12EBDECA99.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, and coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

78F291918C014E8E936DAD818DE25235.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

052EBFBB3E1243BBAA6B010C3290A0E6.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

02B5B5ECC52348BB9E855506117840B8.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

59588094CAD2461390C1A13234218EF3.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

3083C15AA8864C57816304A8F31F470B.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

6C0206353A7341AD96F41D51771572DF.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

1FF0AD91918D4B5EA6606C1856B26D55.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

56C0487AE55844D4A7611FA202C7829A.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

8138BAF637D14A4DB7531EB98D4767C5.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative positions of two numbers on a number line diagram.

A84A918BEE9743D7829957C3D79367A6.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

7021D4793CD84F12950ECD2361F22250.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

5F5DE5443B1D4BD5AC0AC398FCE86A17.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

91A92B82141A43FCA52BCEB50981420C.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that zero is its own opposite.

62C2E046FB274668AC2206A8FEBCA900.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

19CD7340FE464EED9E79EB127C8F2896.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, and positive/negative electric charge). Use positive and negative numbers (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals) to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of zero in each situation.

749BBA359E514D7E9DA22267BD978241.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

18C60D2ABD5F4F4386214E79F9AD2D40.description: Use prime factorization to find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two relatively prime numbers.

45FB9820C108478484CFA1BCF585AFEE.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

27D39589AF24418E9666EA586F988761.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

E4345038DA2A47B1BC1360BD66A7B338.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

8D7FDB8387234F12AE99BB36CA92190E.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

8056A7AD2F564BA2B5887D7778B6DDE8.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

A1E43C39C3C2472DB39220E731F02467.description: Solve problems that relate the mass of an object to its volume.

100BD9FB213F4F19B4398A2914978C63.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units within and between measurement systems; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

26CCBB88E97041AAA4DB93D1509AEA8D.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30∕100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

F80A6474DCA54EC5B0E056382DA0F1DA.description: Solve unit rate problems, including those involving unit pricing, and constant speed.

79E17153A63A4516AF0A8ECD55A423E9.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements. Find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

2669B67315E3452CB141452B54DC6F1D.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

605D031448014D11B05A6133F5375553.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship, including the use of units.

3FB7EF6505C04BB78A9B1393BB33B290.description: Understand the concept of a ratio including the distinctions between part:part and part:whole and the value of a ratio; part/part and part/whole. Use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

ACF5CED45CCA4331A7477D6DFF19CE0B.description: Understand ratio and rate concepts and use ratio and rate reasoning to solve problems.

BD71629654A84B28B1E0843F19CEB062.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface areas of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

12527C34F4E741468E7DA31A94D62DBA.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

67BC282805CE45B29A118DD8C97C060A.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = lwh and V = Bh to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

8ECBCDE95ADE4E1D84C40F21853B54F7.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

A97DFDC543E24AD58157132C1918FA26.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

3363509D754D44B7A3087C14F1DADEC5.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

436E76B712BD4ECC9145246F7D0E29FD.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5B90E1C355304BD48EEA6B21A9A6CCF9.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

81BB7E1CD2EF4CCE9FFB0752E85FE76E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Rhode Island Core Standards for Mathematics

1777E4D7BEE64D25B12AE504BDA82B88.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

21D9D44ADED14D208CFD3C6F62E5F177.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

1DBFD70F877A49D38A906D0679B45371.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

956566476CBC4B819337AB32F845AACC.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

377580B599144D8F8F30F079E5892518.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

49BA59D2C4BB41F5A648B66399105051.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

121DA897D77D4880A710DF16CC34735D.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

5489721CCD1F4666AE53E459F1A429EC.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

64CD4AA5FE9F46A0A2AB76FEE61184B5.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

B5CF18D259974C8099B63FCC19B317C7.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

E77A617294F5450A9E9166CE0A086CE9.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

B129BE1A1A2946F591108DF5C402C401.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

12BADA29803F4A909FA0E108C46603F9.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

1B6BD80D21764BA0B39B919730529A34.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

C2B3BE19CB94480E8810124741E0D602.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; Generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

6F5C57433DDE42E5993C43437970FF47.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

9AB4C29F715D49ADBAF345A0656ACE06.description: Extend analysis of patterns to include analyzing, extending, and determining an expression for simple arithmetic and geometric sequences (e.g., compounding, increasing area), using tables, graphs, words, and expressions.

DB206690BC504E568C0D23EDA460AD80.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

5D68CB46882245CA9F4C3F76A868965F.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x ÷ q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

609F1886592F4685B4AE83C48ECE204F.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

C499E628FD2040C6AD8CD83A36175216.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

0DA6309EA1434E308A9F5864ABA03746.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

B594B553755E47E587C6C31F666628F7.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

B623FCCBC6594689B2859A2382F5B21D.description: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

7C8992E6A0944A8D9D2381780AEDAD5B.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

D7F81F83703944F59F713F27953F115F.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with integers and other rational numbers.

F43C0A518C934CFAB8C2382B515A148D.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

BAFBEFCF535247B3A8469281F58BEA0C.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

0E874CFED44B4D06A077589CA11C05FC.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p∕q) = (–p)∕q = p∕(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

4BCCCD76D6E1480EA5376000F5BCAEA1.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

6B816A9BEE7A41C5A74A2E183AE92B33.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide integers and other rational numbers.

233221BD1F8B411586F992FE52D56BC9.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

0C86ED5E728C47C5911AA0773A78BA64.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

56B0F4B955034246B537C639F6855D43.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real- world contexts.

338D4ACBE3C14B1D946111B400732BB8.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make zero.

3600C5F1807E4404B7FFAAD12E40A474.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract integers and other rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

A949F13BBF1945739F430517B933F4A4.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

25DFE59CE4A0496B844AB39F9B7B4F0A.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multi-step ratio, rate, and percent problems.

679472804FF54C7EAAC3EA7DF641004D.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

D81351100659416999209C40B652207F.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

2D10A4CF124F4070A11192F7FD3B99E2.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table, or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

5BD31C2B83BE4C8388D361DFFE7F4504.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

BFEAC17D1E5948F39ADC058F1EF58EB2.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities measured in like or different units.

7B6D66819E6A46889E736C08D18618D2.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

0F1A18A0028D482FBA09C9C3A30BFA83.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

AE683E3B857946929E5B0DBFBC004C4C.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write simple equations and use them to solve for an unknown angle in a figure.

268A6EB4E7B142E38E2924B18AB5B91B.description: Give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

2C8B56612B6444AB891A110326233C33.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.

007DD5CEF9284FA9812B385F5FBE41ED.description: Understand and describe the relationship among the radius, diameter, and area of a circle.

E187D286BBAC46C78BFF0C793C87E71C.description: Understand and describe the relationships among the radius, diameter, and circumference of a circle.

8928775E547C44D5B5EE63CD64E19191.description: Know that a circle is a two-dimensional shape created by connecting all of the points equidistant from a fixed point called the center of the circle.

EFAC41E79615479AAC35FA6077280373.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

5CBD17F310FB44CD8DA7113D36E57603.description: Describe the shape of the two-dimensional face of the figure that results from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

FFDFE0F2D7FA4FC4B380F4D879BF5E08.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) two-dimensional geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

71A0F39A8EDB490ABA279AA14DAD3855.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, such as computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

A99EB5D8C3FF41F2AA786AE9CA9A9A2E.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

61D9B471760F43E09160563218D648E7.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

CA702D0489E84113832AE9200381DC22.description: Look for and make use of structure.

00BF29BD84044869B8A75B1B23C7DDDE.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

30129927C4544B5591D752F8A82C444B.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Rhode Island Core Standards for Mathematics

C29382BF1EB94C7DB9BCDE7EA3E53A29.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

EFDD80404E104326957D3AB2EA07FC0C.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

F008A743777A4EB1936AC135C0A86F33.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

AA995A5413C143A68EF635568653AB68.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

180AC790D38F4AA69AE6675A6FB41471.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

B2DB114421C6489CB98B5512A87C8E78.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

3665D3CEF07E47D39B77FB5C3AFB0B07.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

761ED79D631841BA9BBE1D2D3DFB8D91.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

B4F194C4952348E9B310B8FEC5318F51.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

1E8295FBACA84C688A52C7D56DAAE6D8.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

81707601FD444ECFAFE3DF43E4F2A238.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

005087E1A87C484986AAF9DCBAEE2496.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

9ABC37ECB36A465BB21D46DE9852101C.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically (using substitution and elimination strategies), and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.

BF7AEEAA3E8B494C9C93D6F23C13FAF1.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

1442B9990AC6451B9CA0BD2FED491C46.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

98CC7EBB9371430E9620E8EBEA90CF15.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

D8051FD8677C4915BEF53D0DA80D5BED.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

060577896B7640D5ADDFFAB378D5243C.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

205CCF2F438547F39E57F990569C7EFC.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

B547FF8ECF754086947B4691E39F8D6C.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non- vertical line in the coordinate plane. Derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

48498DCA405248B683295B13DE9ABE9D.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

20A7209F834A4AD792E9B926F647DBD0.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

C5B3DC2DA875468AB1B5E8E92F157AB3.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

9D962233844944ED81BF59DD42ADF87D.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit multiplied by an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and express how many times as much one is than the other.

C72C8B1BC1454F3DBD8AED23ED2C9A3A.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that is irrational.

F340B27EC53C48CDB5CFD0202B3FE490.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

4463E04AFD294995A2632877671BD078.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

A30500EADB1546B294AD910F119FBF3A.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

2EDE25BBB82B42399ACCC4BB458DC2C9.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion. For rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

B4FFA88DA4534818997C2F72747E4120.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

FEC35E416DE446D39DD54861FF8DBB63.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres, and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

D224EA529F964BBCA1480DC629204426.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

B49275BE68264BDB9FCA57C7A5C063DC.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

5DEAF0BE80F340ACAE6D45266392309F.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

C37C53282996473A95BBBEE9DBFF2F0E.description: Analyze and justify the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse using pictures, diagrams, narratives, or models.

046874E6A29B4F3294EDC39E1B730C08.description: Understand the relationship among the sides of a right triangle.

C9F955B5BC284748B096EA17ED8BFEB9.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

06C854FC93194F6CB487C31C8371A7BC.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.

F8EBEB2555B141D2AF943465E226E725.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations. Given two similar two- dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

36B11ECB40D241D6A5F3BBD0D8BA9FE8.description: Describe the effects of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

8F021BB406EC44D3980294A4CE4542E1.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations. Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

53215AC8419D45928AAA22666905708E.description: Parallel lines are transformed to parallel lines.

8B9A1928724A42CC9AF09408ADA29178.description: Angles are transformed to angles of the same measure.

4B721AD7D26D45599C74992620EE4038.description: Lines are transformed to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

12DCED33459D416BB9DA6FFCA678E260.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

498218E99B7A407991495789E0C15136.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

72374DC84089457B9C96E10A4A34A1FE.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

440967E180224D3AB400E33371320DA0.description: Look for and make use of structure.

B0FB97051CB841C19565EA483E632EED.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

66A48E24339048CE9DE897E0319ABE5C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Rhode Island Core Standards for Mathematics

22DC703B5318402BBBC927E27854E552.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, or pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game and replacing the goalie with an extra skater).★

F2DA8F78F96D482BA1DB5B4CD4E4553F.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots or using a random number generator).★

CD38F355FCD446D69E5E5C0FAE797852.description: (+) Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.★

DEE1B46DB8E04F4A9EEDB371E85488B0.description: (+) Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.★

68584CC0BB2742DB897364DD34D651C9.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.★

F551428CEBA240BCA22FFAF4251128ED.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

BA11B9E6B7A14B1BB9869C093AA0C891.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.★

30799D541EB94D49937AF44761252621.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.★

FB775041A94344DF9D89CA2B9EE6FBEB.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.★

A5AFC35388DC4FE5A4748F5A305A7DB2.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.★

FAAB42586C194F40911F9A513E9197D0.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

BE8546A5C71C49C8AB1662C09059305C.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.★

4B3313703F344567A74CB90031FB4CDB.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.★

F0091FA2975F4CA392F974E03EE0CF66.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.★

3BF43577E2784C16A4135367CE16DF04.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.★

8D92873F98524A7CA1179D11F99BDB74.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

81A6E08F1FBE4690A252287073D67AE1.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.★

85A40AFB4E1C4DB884956F37BF4F2ABD.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.★

312ED19D3E2E4414B74B0B11622CD61F.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.★

A06A0844966B45D388255FB5A959F8DD.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.★

CC651339845349908592CFB50A5C8E63.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").★

749DAE6B710A496ABFE7AC2D4C030989.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data from simulations or experiments.

E36882E524FA42C591845C9B747516E8.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

442364F85E5C46D6AD3E2BC29F69BBE3.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.★

06CE1C6043D64178B088D8350680A357.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.★

4A9E5D7CEF40468FAEB898F511D4C1BF.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.★

09963D42C50C4A67AFE8F04738DB1070.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

F34B64529EBD4755A71E2AC932D285E0.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process (e.g., using simulation).★

D0CFCDAD6564427A8E6055265D1DD364.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.★

9D1754B17E9C44CF8B4420CB56B8C793.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and other technology as appropriate.

112B00F5D71A49B38673C69FBF01224C.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.★

A98ED65D212F4E02A72736377D865EA1.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.★

18FAB2830BAD46149372B040103497DF.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.★

02E3C42167144FB693282BC1A4AA6BF4.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.★

8CCF336C626A4B8CA49AFC2A723576CE.description: Fit a linear function to the data and use the fitted function to solve problems in the context of the data. Use functions fitted to data or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.★

C37A7F3376724EE1993A3E588C24C764.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.★

E33E5778CA024078A865BD52AECF180C.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.★

2BB5E026B3CA4BCF9CA00BD6AA4C585B.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

A45B4F2C8FD54DEB8160C5F525366277.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.★

2A23A74682C04459B6777B6658A877BD.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).★

088E630EF0CD45C29D89B0BC0A1254CC.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.★

9A0E2AD98B7A439A9BD8191F0B2463D4.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).★

2180DFC037854BB58F97879C39B9175F.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and other technology as appropriate.

D81159C150864DEFA31D7B1C0A26CFE7.description: Use dimensional analysis for unit conversions to confirm that expressions and equations make sense.★

76E22D7FA2414506BCA3AED8D401407E.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).★

254AC8A3215148D78AE6E5555E363D1A.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).★

D23D4829F3F449958120657E34F364BF.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).★

31EE0AC8A5A94B77AC725F82E5E4CDF6.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

07D1C0A0799A4964AC07C4D500F2432C.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three- dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

9B57E38A6A5D4B1CB0974ACD3B6C4003.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

79E44DA045164C7F8DB4B68B30963920.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.★

4B110AF51970473FBB35D7E1BFAF206B.description: (+) Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

4A7CA99016ED4A7BBDF8B7DE04800FD3.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

851C5F0ACDFF4B2CA6F0154A69999247.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

AFC6F23BEBB94D61B3827D2F897ACA39.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles (e.g., using the distance formula).★

0293F43731B44B009B8F3049B8D1BA7C.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

0EF3F424B3E54BAAABDB31CD6A10F3A1.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

51CE2496D85B418CB0E6547EE2B1A102.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically including the distance formula and its relationship to the Pythagorean Theorem.

3FED76F4DAB54E79BB127FC0EFE038DB.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

615FF66744F348DB987FBBB1C12CF1D6.description: (+) Use equations and graphs of conic sections to model real-world problems.★

38DBA19A44ED496C9E5E86C7FDC4C7D3.description: (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

0C6A7238CB344238881A896C5659F6E3.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

F3F54A6E91E247DCA126017681AE7678.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

03B66EEC0C42458185FD676E633F7A39.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

10F8B36FEAF945AFBD52196DFC785D59.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

54507562BF6B4777AD48EFC0F74962F7.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

134E3AD28DE54D88BA96ABA9C3B1F44F.description: (+) Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

4AA655BEB06140A6837E61CEA1D2AEC9.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral and other polygons inscribed in a circle.

DE6AA9DFA43B438BBDA887A06EBDE49A.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. 6066C588BF1B48D191A6451EB0F32E89.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

7C6A04E6B01648E0B2C05B9DF8C0F0AD.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

29F18B9B6E57498CB7523B351AD14FA3.description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

93DF242C872740DBB3A2F27C486252CE.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

FD9F7F4E022D4A46ABF8ACD2F05786EB.description: (+) Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

35DC7540E09F4E3FB7DDD882922C135B.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.★

F61D4BA5C7BF48358A170B04390A7D7F.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

DBDBFE99695C4F3DB7000637A8F95AA3.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

83D691D935B54CC8B2FF46FE0AB6FD5B.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

C57A8CAE902E46D2A7854E74566A7BA5.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

552AB0B699374E85B87108C391BD1D19.description: Argue how the relationship between populations and physical systems influence decision-making about the equitable access to resources and land at the local, regional, and/or global levels.

0AC7679476374A4998FBB3AD3FD1A5D8.description: Analyze how human systems and the distribution of populations interact with and impact physical systems, and how conflict and access to resources influence physical systems.

4CD059BE594447B18F8045C90972CDEE.description: Explain how and why a population's characteristics, including their spatial distribution, growth, and movement, have divided, organized, and unified areas of Earth's surface and impacted both human and physical systems.

C3C563AD48694C8E8D8D629D5BCB7EE6.description: Identify the characteristics of populations based on their size, place, region, and cultural demographics, as well as identifying patterns of migration.

23C929DF16C64D26979EE75E2714941F.description: Argue how all individuals can act as local, national, and/or global agents of social change by using lessons learned from history.

4FCDC59862044FF8BD038CFFE404E5BC.description: Analyze historical change through the intersectional identities and lived experiences of people who have accomplished social change throughout history in relation to systems of power, identity, and resistance.

5BA18714841C409D8BC8FFC883DEDEFE.description: Explain how historical and social change have been and continue to be accomplished in relation to systems of power, identity, and resistance.

57239CB9680844DDB96E5A04FD97C86A.description: Identify peoples, events, technologies, and ideas involved in historical and social change in various geographical and temporal locations.

F6D38439419049B781999AF034704283.description: Argue, using multiple narratives rooted in identity, power, and resistance, how history itself is an interpretation of events.

D5293D73735E42C58685BCB99E98C33F.description: Analyze multiple types of sources, including art, music, oral histories, pamphlets, film, texts, etc., through a critical reflection of the creators' and students' intersectional identities and lived experiences.

821A1AE003294E1F8F5CF7AD68DA0C90.description: Explain the purpose, audience, and perspective of multiple types of sources (art, music, oral histories, pamphlets, film, texts, etc.) relating to a historical event or series of events, individual, or group of people, including indications of bias toward or against the subject portrayed.

84AB5168A69345458F361DC3F842F7C2.description: Identify key people, central ideas, and the mechanisms by which stories are told and retold regarding an event or series of events, centering the voices of historical actors and groups engaged in resistance and change.

32057E43308D4F159A4919712B4366BF.description: Argue how social change, intersectional identities, and lived experiences are crucial to the study and practice of history.

E6C15C5934BE4FA480D6CB9FD5439F36.description: Analyze multiple sources to compare and contrast historical events through the lenses of identity, power, and resistance.

BB8F7AD05A2A4E9FAF3EE6B58AEE2770.description: Explain multiple causes and effects of historical events, centering and representing the voices and experiences of individuals and communities who were agents of change and resistance.

BB0C3DC07CE34598AD21469677D2522E.description: Identify historical events that are culturally relevant to global, national, and local histories and connect to students' intersectional identities and lived experiences.

951770B7AE4E40949274169D55EBB6AE.description: Argue for a possible solution to make rights equitable and the roles of those involved in pursuing that solution.

0763C00F3FD54B96A45BEC0705AAEF12.description: Analyze how individuals and communities have been included or excluded from the political process based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences and the impact these actions have had on their rights, responsibilities, and the functioning of a democratic society.

7C1C31046FB04162A3CB63FA49E74CDB.description: Explain different ways communities and individuals inform themselves, exercise their rights and responsibilities, and engage formally and/or informally in political processes.

148E3497C0CE4F1F9F9A22ACD2A4635C.description: Identify what rights and responsibilities individuals and communities have in a society and who can take advantage of them.

191C33E3BFB6455B89151F0B324B2E76.description: Argue how rules and laws can be used to create an equitable society.

0C3A1CEA04C244609751818C8AA43DD9.description: Analyze how rules and laws positively and/or negatively impact different individuals and communities based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences.

D317D96871DE4258B925F15244B29336.description: Explain why rules and laws exist, and how they are implemented by and for individuals and communities based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences.

6DFF33A567DB4D7D941DFADF200BB7EE.description: Identify what rules and laws are, and who has the power to make them, in different settings and cultures that are familiar and unfamiliar to students.

A2E77EB322284EF485F08AEFC18E479E.description: Argue how power can be distributed and used to create a more equitable society for communities and individuals based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences.

7DFD342FBAEF447C9BC7F6DE5AD841A7.description: Analyze the purpose of government and the use of power, including balancing order and freedom, to advance and control different communities and individuals based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences.

8FCA9B15BEF643A2B24B81ED74DC3D4B.description: Explain how political power is and has been obtained and used to govern communities and individuals with attention to their intersectional identities and lived experiences.

FC90CB90F3D84E44ACABB97517B22BE4.description: Identify what political power is and who has political power in a society.

FBD13A9FC0A54C54A96CC1E8310AF852.description: Explain multiple causes and effects of historical events, centering and representing the voices and experiences of individuals and communities who were agents of change and resistance.

7002D4634731436CAC88A768E02FB727.description: Analyze how rules and laws positively and/or negatively impact different individuals and communities based on their intersectional identities and lived experiences.
